title: Integrate allowlisted OTP request/verify snippet into backend/main.mo (upgrade-safe) without breaking existing admin OTP endpoints

requirements.text: In `backend/main.mo`, add new public canister methods equivalent to the user-provided snippet: `requestOtp(identifier : Text)` and `verifyOtp(identifier : Text, enteredOtp : Text)` that implement an allowlisted admin identifier OTP flow (identifier can be phone or email). These new methods must not rename/remove or change the signatures of the existing endpoints `requestAdminOtp`, `verifyAdminOtp`, or `validateAdminSession`.

quotes: Isko main.mo me daal do ---import Principal "mo:base/Principal"; ... public shared func requestOtp(identifier: Text) ... public shared func verifyOtp(identifier: Text, enteredOtp: Text) ...

acceptanceCriteria: `backend/main.mo` still compiles with the existing `requestAdminOtp`, `verifyAdminOtp`, and `validateAdminSession` functions intact (same names and parameter lists).
A new `requestOtp(identifier : Text)` method exists and is callable.
A new `verifyOtp(identifier : Text, enteredOtp : Text)` method exists and is callable.

requirements.text: Implement allowlist enforcement for the newly added `requestOtp`/`verifyOtp` methods using a hardcoded list of authorized admin identifiers (phone/email) as shown in the snippet. If an identifier is not allowlisted, the methods must reject with English error messages (do not return Hindi user-facing strings).

quotes: return #err("Yeh number/email admin ke liye allowed nahi hai");

acceptanceCriteria: Calling `requestOtp` with a non-allowlisted identifier returns an error with an English message indicating the identifier is not allowed.
Calling `verifyOtp` with a non-allowlisted identifier returns an error with an English message indicating the identifier is not allowed.

requirements.text: For the new OTP flow (`requestOtp`/`verifyOtp`), generate and store a 6-digit OTP per identifier with a 10-minute expiry using `Time.now()` and delete the OTP entry after successful verification or after detecting expiration. Return a success result from `requestOtp` that includes the OTP for testing (as in the snippet), but ensure the returned message is in English.

quotes: #ok("OTP bhej diya gaya: " # otp # " (testing ke liye screen par dikhega)")
if (now > expiry) { otpStorage.delete(identifier); #err("OTP expire ho gaya"); } else if (storedOtp == enteredOtp) { otpStorage.delete(identifier); ... }

acceptanceCriteria: `requestOtp` stores an OTP tied to the identifier and sets expiry to `Time.now() + 600_000_000_000` (10 minutes in nanoseconds).
`verifyOtp` returns an error if no OTP exists for that identifier.
`verifyOtp` returns an error if the OTP is expired and removes the stored entry.
`verifyOtp` returns success only when the OTP matches and removes the stored entry.
`requestOtp` returns a success message in English that includes the generated OTP for testing.

requirements.text: Make the storage for the newly added OTP flow upgrade-safe. Because Motoko stable variables cannot directly hold `Map`/`HashMap` structures used at runtime, store OTP entries in a stable representation (e.g., a stable array/list of (identifier, otp, expiry) tuples) and rebuild the in-memory structure in upgrade hooks (e.g., `system func preupgrade()` / `system func postupgrade()`).

quotes: stable var otpStorage = HashMap.HashMap<Text, (Text, Int)>(0, Text.equal, Text.hash);

acceptanceCriteria: OTP entries created via `requestOtp` persist across a canister upgrade (they remain available to `verifyOtp` after upgrade) until they expire or are verified.
The chosen stable representation uses stable-compatible types only (e.g., `Text`, `Int`/`Nat`, `Time.Time`) and does not attempt to store `Map`/`HashMap` directly as `stable`.

requirements.text: Add an admin-protected example method in `backend/main.mo` equivalent to the snippet’s `adminOnlyAction()`, with all returned/trap strings in English. The authorization rule must be clear and must not rely on the snippet’s placeholder principal; it should use an explicit rule such as rejecting anonymous callers or reusing existing admin checks already present in the canister.

quotes: public shared ({ caller }) func adminOnlyAction() : async Text {
if (Principal.isAnonymous(caller)) { "Admin nahi ho" } else { "Admin dashboard access granted!" }

acceptanceCriteria: `adminOnlyAction()` exists and returns English user-facing text.
`adminOnlyAction()` enforces a clear authorization policy (e.g., anonymous callers are rejected/denied, or admin role is required).

constraints: Backend must remain a single-actor Motoko canister; keep all logic in `backend/main.mo`.
Do not break compilation of existing admin OTP/session endpoints already present in `backend/main.mo` (`requestAdminOtp`, `verifyAdminOtp`, `validateAdminSession`).
Use English for any user-facing text (success/error messages) added by this change.
nonGoals: Do not modify the frontend OTP flows as part of this change.
Do not replace or refactor the existing `requestAdminOtp`/`verifyAdminOtp` implementation unless required to resolve naming/type collisions introduced by adding `requestOtp`/`verifyOtp`.
Do not introduce third-party authentication beyond existing Internet Identity usage.
